nodes.label: Firestore/Storage security rules
nodes.rationale: Both apps hit Firestore/Storage directly, so the rules are the only thing keeping users apart; every client-accessed collection needs a rule.

nodes.label: Docker Compose deployment (nginx client + server)
nodes.rationale: Client is built with client/.env baked in and nginx proxies /api, so VITE_API_URL is ignored; it connects to the live project and broker, so stop other server instances first.

nodes.label: Server integration suite (Firebase emulators demo-grownex + in-process MQTT)
nodes.norm_label: server integration suite (firebase emulators demo-grownex + in-process mqtt)

nodes.label: Local sandbox (emulators + sandbox.js broker + fake node ESP32-MOB01)
nodes.norm_label: local sandbox (emulators + sandbox.js broker + fake node esp32-mob01)
nodes.rationale: Lets you click around both apps against emulators instead of the live project and real hardware.

nodes.label: Firestore as the integration point
nodes.rationale: Both clients read/write Firestore directly with live listeners and never talk to devices; mqttBridge is the only MQTT speaker, mirroring device traffic into Firestore and turning Firestore changes into device commands.

nodes.label: Web <-> mobile hand-ported parity
nodes.rationale: The two clients implement the same features separately (zoneFit, plantHealth, aiSummary, analytics, device claiming, CameraCard, StatusLabel), so hand-ported logic must change on both sides together.

nodes.label: FCM push to fcmTokens (mobile only)
nodes.rationale: Sent after the Firestore write without awaiting so FCM latency never delays callers; dead tokens pruned.

nodes.label: users/{uid} (notificationPrefs, fcmTokens)
nodes.rationale: Write with merge: true everywhere, or the FCM tokens get wiped.

nodes.label: expectConfirmation (unconfirmed manual on, CONFIRM_MS 15 s)
nodes.rationale: A silently dropped device still looks online for ~20 s, so a manual toggle can reach a dead device and its retained 'on' would fire on reconnect; unconfirmed ons are switched back off with a warning. isOwnEcho separates bridge writes from manual toggles.

nodes.label: failSafe: relays off while WiFi/MQTT down
nodes.norm_label: failsafe: relays off while wifi/mqtt down
nodes.rationale: Every relay switches off when disconnected; retry every 10 s, restart after 10 min offline; reconnecting re-delivers the retained command which restores the intended state.

nodes.label: Intent (*Active) vs confirmed (*Confirmed) actuator state
nodes.rationale: *Active is intent written by clients/automation, *Confirmed is device-reported via handleActuatorState; writing *Active from device-state handling creates a publish feedback loop. publishCommand syncs actuatorCache first so the Firestore echo doesn't re-publish.

nodes.label: Bottom navigation (Dashboard, Plants/Zones, Analytics, Devices, Profile)
nodes.norm_label: bottom navigation (dashboard, plants/zones, analytics, devices, profile)

nodes.label: UI requirements (compact cards, quick monitoring, mobile-first)
nodes.norm_label: ui requirements (compact cards, quick monitoring, mobile-first)
nodes.rationale: Avoid overcrowded layouts and prioritize readability and quick monitoring; use expandable sections or tabs for detail pages.

nodes.label: Account deletion (DELETE /api/auth/me + mobile fallback)
nodes.rationale: Mobile falls back to the same cleanup in auth_service.dart when the server is unreachable, so the two must be kept in step.

nodes.norm_label: legacy sensorreadings/ and hourly stats/ collections

nodes.label: Sketch: notifications/{notificationId} (global)
nodes.rationale: Global, not nested under zone/user, for easy querying.

nodes.label: Sketch: zones/{zoneId}/sensorReadings (high volume)
nodes.rationale: High volume, so kept separate from the zone document.

nodes.label: Sketch: zones/{zoneId} (core dashboard entity)
nodes.rationale: Kept top-level rather than nested under the user.

nodes.label: Hand-written cascading deletes (ZONE_SUBCOLLECTIONS)
nodes.rationale: Firestore does not delete subcollections and client-side deletes can't list them, so each cascade (web ZoneDetailPage, mobile zone_detail_screen, server auth.js) uses a named list that must be updated for any new subcollection.

nodes.label: Client-maintained cross-document integrity
nodes.rationale: Nothing enforces integrity server-side: zones.deviceId <-> devices.assignedZoneId (and cameraDeviceId) must change together, copying hasLight/hasFertilizer/totalPlantSlots.

nodes.label: Rule-based AI fallback (source: 'fallback')
nodes.rationale: AI is optional: with no API key or on any model/validation error endpoints return fallback and clients keep local rule-based output; fallbackPlan builds a plan with no model.

nodes.label: APPLY_STANDARD_SETTINGS (Linux)
nodes.rationale: Shared compile settings (C++14, -Wall -Werror, -O3/NDEBUG outside Debug) that plugins also use by default, so new options should go on specific targets instead.

nodes.label: flutter_assemble target (Linux, tool_backend.sh)
nodes.rationale: Uses a non-existent _phony_ output so the Flutter tool backend runs on every build, since the tool gives no full input/output list.

nodes.label: list_prepend()
nodes.rationale: Stand-in for list(TRANSFORM ... PREPEND ...), which CMake 3.10 lacks.

nodes.label: APPLY_STANDARD_SETTINGS (Windows)
nodes.rationale: C++17, /W4 /WX, _HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0; applied to the runner and both C++ wrapper libraries.

nodes.label: Linux GTK APPLICATION_ID com.example.mobile_app
nodes.rationale: Unchanged Flutter scaffold placeholder ID; binary name is mobile_app.

nodes.label: Linux relocatable install bundle
nodes.rationale: Executable is built into intermediates_do_not_run because only the installed bundle (lib/ via $ORIGIN rpath, data/flutter_assets, icudtl.dat, AOT libapp.so on non-Debug) has resources in the right relative locations.

nodes.label: Windows in-place install next to executable
nodes.norm_label: windows in-place install next to executable
nodes.rationale: Support files are copied next to the executable instead of a separate bundle (as on Linux) so building and running from Visual Studio works; install is part of the default build.

nodes.label: Nightly job dailySummary.js (evening summary + pruning)
nodes.rationale: Importing dailySummary.js calls getStorage().bucket(), so a missing FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET breaks bridge startup.

nodes.label: reconcileCommands on startup/reconnect
nodes.rationale: Compares broker retained commands with stored intent so changes made while the bridge was down still reach devices.

nodes.label: statsDaily/{YYYY-MM-DD} hourly history docs
nodes.rationale: One doc per UTC day so 7 days of charts cost 8 reads instead of 168; the only sensor history, read by analytics and plant-health scoring on both clients.

nodes.label: Threshold watering (30-min per-device cooldown)
nodes.rationale: Cooldown also stored in devices.lastAutoWateringAt so a restart doesn't water the same dry soil again.

nodes.label: AI output validation (validateSummary/validatePlan/validatePlantProfile)
nodes.rationale: Model output is untrusted, so it is clamped and sanitized; automation-plan never writes Firestore, the client saves the plan after the user confirms.

nodes.label: Firestore Spark free-tier budget
nodes.rationale: 50k reads / 20k writes / 20k deletes per day; each 5-min reading costs 3 writes + 2 reads, ~860 writes per device per day, so ~23 always-on devices fit. Automation config comes from a listener cache to avoid reads.

nodes.label: Single bridge instance (fixed client ID grownex-bridge)
nodes.norm_label: single bridge instance (fixed client id grownex-bridge)
nodes.rationale: Starting the server touches the live project and hardware; with a fixed MQTT client ID two instances kick each other off, double-fire schedules and send duplicate notifications.

nodes.label: TZ / server local time for schedules
nodes.norm_label: tz / server local time for schedules
nodes.rationale: Schedule crons and the summary's 'today' run in server local time, so TZ must be the growers' timezone; Docker and most hosts default to UTC.

nodes.label: forget command (clears retained messages)
nodes.rationale: Without forget, the broker keeps the boards' last retained messages and the server recreates the devices next time it starts.

nodes.label: ESP32-CAM brownout resets (needs 5V/2A supply)
nodes.rationale: Camera plus WiFi peaks above what many USB ports deliver.

nodes.label: In-memory timers lost on server restart
nodes.norm_label: in-memory timers lost on server restart
nodes.rationale: Cron jobs, cooldowns, debounce/confirmation timers and auto-off setTimeouts are in memory; a restart (incl. node --watch reload) loses the pending off and the retained command keeps the actuator on.

nodes.label: Pump hard safety limit (flash-persisted latch)
nodes.rationale: Irrigation 20 min / fertilizer 40 min, counted from the on command including offline time; latch and runtime kept in flash so a reboot with a stale retained 'on' can neither restart the pump nor its countdown. Set above validatePlan's caps so configured runs never reach it.
